Demand thesis STRENGTHENED on every axis in Q2 and nothing regime-related breaks it. Already at the +2 ceiling; the open question is whether these dollars survive capex to reach owner earnings (that is M4).

Two offsetting moves, net held +1. IMPROVED: the central incremental-moat test ('can post-AI-capex capital earn high returns?') got its first real yes -- Cloud held a ~35.5% margin across a second quarter on a $513.9B backlog, and Search durability (+17%) confirms the existing moat is intact under AI pressure; a cheaper-memory regime (SOX -25%, CXMT new DRAM supply) helps GOOGL as a compute BUYER, not a seller. WORSE: capex guidance RAISED to $195-205B (2027 higher) into a NEGATIVE-FCF quarter with still no disclosed ROI hurdle (CFO 'attractive return' is a philosophy, not a number); buybacks $0, ~$18B mandatory convertible preferred + debt issued, and 52.7% founder voting power means no external lever on the capex bet. Operator grade unchanged ~28/40. Existing moat Strong and better-evidenced; incremental moat partly-but-not-fully proven; capital-allocation discipline still absent.

WORSENED -1 -> -2: the June warning MATERIALIZED. Q2 free cash flow went NEGATIVE -$5.9B (vs +$10.1B Q1'26, +$5.3B Q2'25); TTM FCF fell to ~$53.3B (-20% YoY); capex a record $44.9B (~115% of quarterly OCF; TTM capex/OCF ~71%, crossing the 70% line); FCF/share ~$4.36 TTM vs $6.06 FY25 (-28%) while share count ROSE (12,088M -> 12,230M) with buybacks at $0 and ~$18B preferred + debt issued. Meanwhile GAAP net income printed $112B (+298%) on a ~$99B non-cash unrealized equity-securities gain (~$6.26 of the $9.11 EPS) -> reported income overstates owner earnings ~2.6-4.4x; owner earnings ~$55-95B (defensive-to-growth read). Not fraud and not a survival risk (liquidity huge, dividend + growth capex are by choice); Cloud's ~35.5% margin is a real growth-read offset -- but the specific capex-black-hole mechanism has begun to realize, so the signal must worsen to a strong warning (not a veto).

Held -1 with the picture clarified by Q2 + the 7/28 regime. The scariest PERMANENT path was F1xF3 confluence (AI erodes search AND capex balloons -> owner earnings permanently diluted). Q2 SPLIT the legs: F3 (capex black hole) MATERIALIZED (FCF negative, guide raised), but F1 (search erosion) was DISCONFIRMED (Search +17%, AI additive) and F2 (regulatory) EASED (DOJ search resolved WITHOUT a breakup, on appeal; DOJ adtech judge skeptical of a structural AdX divestiture, ruling still pending as of as_of; EC fine on appeal). REGIME overlay (7/28 semiconductor crash / AI-capex-audit year / rotation out of AI-hardware / CXMT DRAM entrant / FOMC Wed): the capex audit is precisely GOOGL's binding question, so the market is LESS forgiving of the raised capex (the -7% earnings reaction is that audit in action); but GOOGL is NOT a memory/Korea/merchant-silicon name -- as a compute BUYER a cheaper-hardware regime is mildly favorable, so CXMT/SOX hit it only via multiple/sentiment, not fundamentals. FOMC/higher-for-longer would raise the discount rate on a long-duration ~1.7%-yield asset -> a near-term multiple swing, not a thesis break. Net: a capex/VALUATION trap made more acute by the regime, not a franchise-death spiral -> haircut/size driver (-1), not a veto (-2).

runner_dissent: Recorded per protocol, and the tension is real. Q2 genuinely improved the BULL case AND (at the trough) made the stock cheaper -- the missed-compounder risk is larger than in June. Cloud is now demonstrably converting capex into high-margin revenue (~35.5% margin, op income ~tripled, $513.9B backlog, +82% growth) -- exactly the 'incremental ROIC holds' disconfirming evidence the June bear thesis needed -- and the two scariest permanent paths (F1 search erosion, F2 structural regulatory remedy) both weakened. The 7/28 rotation OUT of AI-hardware could also be the very catalyst that eventually delivers a buyable price. The framework nonetheless HOLDS WATCH/0% (does NOT override to STARTER, unlike the NVDA case) because PRICE is the constraint and it got WORSE, not better, since the trough: at $333.71 the base-case 10y IRR is still NEGATIVE (~-1.5%) and, after the +5% bounce, even the bull case (~+7.7%) no longer clears 8% -- you would pay full price for the optimistic case with zero cushion. This quarter the capex-eats-FCF thesis did not just persist, it REALIZED (FCF went negative, FCF/share -28% from peak, dilution now naked, preferred + debt issued, capex raised to $205B with still no ROI hurdle), and on trailing FCF the stock is MORE expensive (~76.6x) than in June. A 9% drop that coincides with a 20% FCF decline is not a margin of safety. Wait for price (~$99-117), not for a better story -- the story is already good.
